card.name: Bagha Nacha (Tiger dance)
card.era: Traditional; performance lineage cited to late 18th century
card.tagline: Striped tiger dancers appease the goddess in Ganjam
card.profile: Bagha Nacha (Tiger Dance) is a folk dance of Odisha performed in Binka and Sonepur (Subarnapur district), Berhampur and parts of Ganjam district, chiefly in the month of Chaitra (March-April) (Wikipedia). Male dancers paint themselves as tigers - a process taking three to four hours and at least two assistants - and dance to dhampa/changu drumbeats as homage to goddess Maa Budhi Thakurani, whose vahana is the tiger. Performers are not necessarily professional dancers; they train two to four weeks under a mentor. Four changus are required, and devotees observe vows, fasting and celibacy (Wikipedia; Hindu Blog).
card.insight: In January 2025 more than 40 male dancers performed Bagha Nacha in the Republic Day parade ensemble organised by the Ministry of Culture, and an Odia feature film on the tradition was released the same month (Wikipedia).
card.image_significance: Odisha's tiger dance of devotion. A representative image shows ceremonial regalia in a ritual context — imagery should be handled respectfully, not as spectacle — Odisha (Ganjam), India.
